title: centaurea ispahanica subsp. macrocarpa
intro: Centaurea ispahanica subsp. macrocarpa, commonly known as a plant species in the aster family, is a flowering perennial native to the Middle East and Mediterranean regions. It has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. The bioactive constituents of Centaurea ispahanica subsp. macrocarpa include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are believed to contribute to its therapeutic actions, such as wound healing, pain relief, and immune system modulation. However, more research is needed to fully understand the effects of this plant on human health.
